title: Twisted-section fraction evaluation respects homogeneous chart restrictions
statement: Let $S=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}S_d$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring and $X=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-pc-proj]. Assume that $X$ is covered by the standard opens $D_+(f)$ with $f\in S_1$. Let $\mathcal F$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Put $\mathcal O_X(n)=\widetilde{S(n)}$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], $\mathcal F(n)=\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_X(n)$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and $N=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}\Gamma(X,\mathcal F(n))$, with the $S$-action given by canonical sections and the unital associative twist multiplication maps of [lem-sfb-standard-proj-twist-tensor]. For every homogeneous $g\in S_d$ with $d>0$, the canonical section $g$ freely generates $\mathcal O_X(d)|_{D_+(g)}$. The formula $\phi_g:N_{(g)}\longrightarrow\Gamma(D_+(g),\mathcal F)$, $t/g^m\longmapsto t|_{D_+(g)}\otimes g^{-m}$, for $m\ge0$ and $t\in N_{md}$, is a well-defined $S_{(g)}$-linear map, where $g^{-m}$ uses the inverse of that trivialization and twist multiplication. For homogeneous $h\in S_b$, $b>0$, with $D_+(g)\subseteq D_+(h)$, let $\rho_{h,g}:N_{(h)}\to N_{(g)}$ be the standard homogeneous localization restriction of [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists]. Then $\phi_g\rho_{h,g}=\operatorname{res}_{D_+(h),D_+(g)}\phi_h$. Explicitly, for any homogeneous relation $g^e=ah$ with $e\ge1$, $a\in S_c$, $c\ge0$, and $ed=c+b$, the map $\rho_{h,g}$ sends $t/h^m$ to $a^mt/g^{em}$, and $\phi_g(a^mt/g^{em})=\bigl(t|_{D_+(h)}\otimes h^{-m}\bigr)|_{D_+(g)}$. The maps and the identity are independent of the choice of fraction representative and of $e,a$. No finite generation of $S$, quasi-compactness of $X$, or quasi-coherence of $\mathcal F$ is assumed.

proof.text: Write $U_g=D_+(g)$. By [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], $g|_{U_g}$ is the fraction $g/1$ and $q_g=1/g$ is a section of $\mathcal O_X(-d)$ on $U_g$. Their twist products are $gq_g=q_gg=1$. Here is a chart check of this assertion, including the sheaf multiplication: on $D_+(f)$, $f\in S_1$, the fraction description identifies $\mathcal O_X(n)$ with the free module generated by $f^n$; this holds on every standard subchart because $f$ is a unit there by [lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion](1). The multiplication formula in [lem-sfb-standard-proj-twist-tensor] sends $f^i\otimes f^j$ to $f^{i+j}$. On $D_+(f)\cap U_g=D_+(fg)$ the two sections have coefficients $g/f^d$ and $f^d/g$ in these frames, whose product is $1$. These intersections cover $U_g$, so the equality holds as a sheaf equality. Multiplication by $g$ and by $q_g$ are therefore mutually inverse sheaf maps between $\mathcal O_{U_g}$ and $\mathcal O_X(d)|_{U_g}$. This proves the asserted free generator. The unital associative products of the same node give $q_g^m\in\Gamma(U_g,\mathcal O_X(-md))$ and mutually inverse maps $\theta_{g,m}:\mathcal F(md)|_{U_g}\to\mathcal F|_{U_g}$, $v\mapsto vq_g^m$, and $w\mapsto wg^m$. Tensor balancing here is exactly [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

proof.text: Define the value on a representative $t/g^m$ to be $\theta_{g,m}(t|_{U_g})$. By the localization relation of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], equality $t/g^m=u/g^n$ means that $g^k(g^nt-g^mu)=0$ in $N$ for some $k\ge0$. Restriction gives $g^{k+n}t|_{U_g}=g^{k+m}u|_{U_g}$ in $\mathcal F((k+m+n)d)(U_g)$. Apply multiplication by $q_g^{k+m+n}$, using Step 1 and the associative twist products of [lem-sfb-standard-proj-twist-tensor]; the result is $t|_{U_g}q_g^m=u|_{U_g}q_g^n$. Thus the value is independent of the representative. For addition the localization formula is $(t/g^m)+(u/g^n)=(g^nt+g^mu)/g^{m+n}$; applying the proposed map gives $t|_{U_g}q_g^m+u|_{U_g}q_g^n$. The zero fraction maps to zero. These operations therefore give an additive map $\phi_g$.

proof.text:
Every scalar in $S_{(g)}$ is a fraction $s/g^r$ with $s\in S_{rd}$ and $r\ge0$, by [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] for the zero twist. Its product with $t/g^m$ is $st/g^{r+m}$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. The twist multiplication of [lem-sfb-standard-proj-twist-tensor] and tensor balancing give
$\phi_g(st/g^{r+m})=(s|_{U_g}t|_{U_g})q_g^{r+m}=(s|_{U_g}q_g^r)(t|_{U_g}q_g^m)=(s/g^r)\phi_g(t/g^m)$.
In the last equality the product of the canonical section $s$ with $q_g^r$ is the fraction $s/g^r$ of the structure sheaf: this is the same local-frame calculation as Step 1 with degrees $rd,-rd$. Consequently $\phi_g$ is $S_{(g)}$-linear.

proof.text:
Suppose $U_g\subseteq U_h$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists](a), choose $e\ge1$ and homogeneous $a$ with $g^e=ah$; increase $e$ by multiplying by powers of $g$ if needed so its homogeneous degree $c=ed-b$ is nonnegative. This node gives the restriction formula $\rho_{h,g}(t/h^m)=a^mt/g^{em}$ and its independence of $e,a$. Restrict $q_h^m$ to $U_g$. In $\mathcal O_X(-mb)(U_g)$ one has $a^mq_g^{em}=q_h^m|_{U_g}$: multiplication by $h^m$ is invertible by Step 1 for $h$, and sends the left side to $(ah)^mq_g^{em}=g^{em}q_g^{em}=1$, and the right side to $1$. All degrees agree since $mc-emd=-mb$. It follows that
$\phi_g(a^mt/g^{em})=t|_{U_g}a^mq_g^{em}=t|_{U_g}(q_h^m|_{U_g})=(t|_{U_h}q_h^m)|_{U_g}$.
Restriction commutes with these tensor products by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and with module operations by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Every element is such a fraction, so this is the desired equality of maps. Step 2 proves independence of both fraction presentations; the displayed equality holds for every admissible $e,a$, so it also proves the asserted choice independence for the evaluation identity. The case $m=0$ uses the unit products. If a chart is empty, all its section modules are zero and the same identities hold. No step used a finite cover, quasi-compactness, or quasi-coherence of $\mathcal F$.

lean.statement: theorem projSectionFractionNaturality (cover : ∀ x : Proj 𝒜, ∃ f ∈ 𝒜 1, x ∈ basicOpen 𝒜 f) (F : (Proj 𝒜).Modules) : (∀ (g : S) (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) (hg : g ∈ 𝒜 d), IsFreeGenerator ((unitToTwist hg).app (basicOpen 𝒜 g) (1 : Γ(Proj 𝒜, basicOpen 𝒜 g)))) ∧ ∃ m : Module S (DirectSum ℤ (fun n : ℤ ↦ Γ(F ⊗ twist 𝒜 n, ⊤))), (∀ (d : ℕ) (n : ℤ) (s : S) (hs : s ∈ 𝒜 d) (t : Γ(F ⊗ twist 𝒜 n, ⊤)), @SMul.smul S (DirectSum ℤ (fun k : ℤ ↦ Γ(F ⊗ twist 𝒜 k, ⊤))) m.toSMul s (DirectSum.of (fun k : ℤ ↦ Γ(F ⊗ twist 𝒜 k, ⊤)) n t) = DirectSum.of (fun k : ℤ ↦ Γ(F ⊗ twist 𝒜 k, ⊤)) (n + d) ((F ◁ twistMul n hs).app ⊤ t)) ∧ @IsProjSectionFractionNaturality S _ 𝒜 _ F m
lean.note: The homogeneous localization is an additive subgroup of the ordinary localization with exactly the homogeneous-fraction carrier. Closure under homogeneous-localization scalars and the scalar equation express linearity without a second scalar instance. Evaluation is characterized by tensoring back with the canonical section g^m, which is equivalent to division by its free generator. The restriction formula is quantified over every degree-compatible relation witness, making choice independence explicit.
